draft.title: Work health and safety
card: In NSW, the Work Health and Safety Act 2011 (NSW) requires a person who runs a business to keep workers safe at work, as far as is reasonably practicable. This is called a duty of care.
The duty covers more than injuries from machines. It includes a safe workplace, safe equipment, safe work systems, and training and supervision.
Workers also have duties. They must take reasonable care for their own safety and must not put others at risk.
SafeWork NSW is the regulator that enforces the Act. It can inspect workplaces, issue notices requiring problems to be fixed, and prosecute those who break the law.
draft.remember: The employer must keep workers safe, and SafeWork NSW enforces the law.

a.q: Which body enforces the Work Health and Safety Act 2011 (NSW) in NSW workplaces?
opts: SafeWork NSW
The Fair Work Commission
The Australian Human Rights Commission
The Fair Work Ombudsman
a.why: SafeWork NSW is the regulator that inspects workplaces and enforces the Act. The Fair Work Commission is tempting because it deals with workplace matters, but it is not the regulator for safety.
a.clue: Which body is named on the card as the regulator?

b.q: Tane runs a warehouse in Parramatta. A forklift has a broken brake, and he lets staff keep using it. Which duty has Tane most clearly failed to meet?
opts: His duty to provide safe equipment for workers
His duty to pay workers the award rate
His duty to avoid discrimination in hiring
His duty to keep workers' personal records private
b.why: A faulty forklift is unsafe equipment, and providing safe equipment is part of the employer's duty of care under the Act. Pay is a different workplace issue and is not what this case is about.
b.clue: Think about what is wrong with the forklift.

b.best: His duty to provide safe equipment for workers
